newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australian bonds to remain under pressure.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australian bonds to remain under pressure.

text.p: *The Australian bond market is expected to continue last week's reversal from two month highs, returning from its long holiday weekend to find that the U.S. Treasury market had succumbed to down sessions in its absence.
*Busy week for data, both locally and the U.S..

The Australian bond futures market is expected to continue last week's reversal from two month highs, although recent favourable domestic data on wages and inflation should keep it from retreating too far.

The market returns from its long holiday weekend for ANZAC Day to find that U.S. Treasuries had succumbed to two down sessions in its absence, leaving the 30-year U.S. bond yield at 7.14 percent, some six basis above Wednesday's New York close.
The June 10-year bond futures contract ended its pre-ANZAC Day SYCOM session at 92.090 compared with Thursday's 92.110 open outcry close.
At its SYCOM close the 10-year contract is in a band of support between 92.100 and 92.080 and a break down here would see a further retracement to 92.030, analysts said.
On the upside there is some resistance at 93.160, but the major area is 92.210/92.230 and a zone that the market failed to make a definite breach of last week.

There is a busy flow of economic data this week, both locally and in the U.S., although the latter is expected to be driving force at the start of the week. March home sales are due Monday, and durable goods orders for the same month and the first quarter employment cost index are due Tuesday.

Australia's own data kicks off on Wednesday with the March balance of goods and services, although the key events will be first quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) and building approvals on Thursday and retail trade on Friday.

As long as AWOTE remains in the Reserve Bank's 4.0 to 4.5 percent comfort zone, weak retail trade and building approvals data may add some fire to recent speculation that the RBA will ease policy again after benign inflation and "living wage" outcomes last week.
Deputy RBA governor Stephen Grenville is due to address a conference in Sydney at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
